assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
caveats: Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level is 92.1%, order-level 94.9% and technical 95.78%. Retries and customer drop-offs explain the gap, so quote which definition you mean.

Some Meridian Bank card attempts in August (931 of 11,537, 8.1%) have no issuer ID, so issuer-level results for that scope are understated. These rows were kept and shown as '(missing)' issuer, not corrected. This affects card scope, and the UPI findings above do not rely on it.
Failure-code figures are per 100 attempts, not shares of failures.
Daily series shown in the evidence only extend to 2 September, so the pattern for 3–10 September is not visible day by day.

facts.text: UPI attempt success rate fell 0.87pp from 92.98% to 92.1% (63,131 attempts in the current window vs 64,606 in the baseline). The change is statistically and practically significant, and the confidence intervals do not overlap.
The mix effect is 0.0pp and the rate effect is -0.87pp, so the entire change is a within-segment rate decline rather than a shift in payment-method mix.
Zephyr is about 30% of UPI volume but accounts for -1.16pp (133%) of the -0.87pp change. Its success rate fell 3.84pp, from 93.4% to 89.6%. Its share of volume barely moved (29.8% to 30.3%).
Other issuers did not fall significantly: Orchid rose 0.66pp, PayNest rose 0.38pp and Tezra rose 0.27pp, none statistically significant.

For Zephyr UPI, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.28 to 3.89 per 100 attempts (53 to 745 failures), a rise of 3.61 per 100 attempts. Other Zephyr failure codes moved by 0.21 per 100 attempts or less.
Across all UPI, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT rose from 0.29 to 1.39 per 100 attempts (189 to 879 failures), the largest increase of any failure code. Other codes moved by 0.15 per 100 attempts or less.

Zephyr's daily success rate was 92.4%–94.5% through 22–31 August, then dropped to 89.9% on 1 September and 88.3% on 2 September. Overall UPI daily rate went from 93.25% on 31 August to 92.6% on 1 September and 91.77% on 2 September.

Smaller rate declines also appear in the no-merchant-group segment (-0.87pp), Saffron Bank (-0.30pp), Meridian Bank (-0.29pp) and the west region (-0.28pp). These are overlapping views of the same attempts, not additive.

response.headline: UPI attempt success rate fell 0.87pp, from 93.0% (22–31 August) to 92.1% (1–10 September). There was no payment-method mix shift (0.0pp); the whole drop is a like-for-like rate decline, concentrated in the Zephyr issuer, whose rate fell 3.84pp.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check Zephyr and PSP incident logs and status pages for 31 August to 2 September. Look at timeout latency by hour from 1 September, and confirm whether any config, routing or release change went live then.
hypotheses.rationale: Zephyr's rate fell sharply, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT is the code that jumped, and the step change coincides with the start of the current window while other issuers were flat or up.
hypotheses.text: A timeout problem in the UPI PSP integration or connectivity for Zephyr-handled transactions, beginning around 1 September, caused the drop.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Zephyr is about 30% of UPI volume but accounts for -1.16pp (133%) of the -0.87pp change.
recommendations.rationale: Timeouts explain most of Zephyr's decline and Zephyr explains more than the whole overall drop.
recommendations.text: Raise the UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT spike with Zephyr and the PSP integration team and ask for an incident review covering 1 September onward.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Zephyr's daily success rate was 92.4%–94.5% through 22–31 August, then dropped to 89.9% on 1 September and 88.3% on 2 September.
recommendations.rationale: The drop started abruptly on 1 September and had not recovered by the last daily data shown (2 September).
recommendations.text: Monitor Zephyr daily UPI success rate and PSP timeout rate per 100 attempts, with an alert if the rate stays below about 92%.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A timeout problem in the UPI PSP integration or connectivity for Zephyr-handled transactions, beginning around 1 September, caused the drop.
recommendations.rationale: Other issuers are stable, so rerouting could recover part of the lost successes while the root cause is fixed.
recommendations.text: Evaluate temporary retry or fallback routing to other UPI issuers or PSPs for timed-out Zephyr attempts, if the business allows it.
